Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back, everyone. The Pakistani players are out in the middle. Saif Hassan and Tanzid Hasan to open for Bangladesh. Shaheen Afridi to bowl first. Let's play...
...THE CHASE...

Game update - Usually, the innings break in this format is longer, but due to the auspicious month of Ramadan, it will be limited to 10 minutes. However, there will be a 40-minute break at 12 pm GMT, allowing the players to break their fast.

Bangladesh's fast bowling coach - Shaun Tait says that they have bowled really well but they still have to chase, and the game is not over. He says that the staff are working hard and the players are doing their best to improve their play. Although it's a positive start for them as they bowled really well in this game, but they need to carry on with this performance. Ended up saying that Nahid Rana has been their standout bowler and he has a lot of potential in him.

The visitors struggled - The new-look Pakistan crumbled under pressure. In the absence of a couple of key players, Pakistan were still expected to put on a competitive performance, but after the solid opening stand, they fell like a pack of cards.  Pakistan managed to cross the 100-mark, thanks to the cameo from Faheem Ashraf, but it probably would not bail them out of a certain result. Pakistan need a miracle, and the opening ten overs could predict the future of this game, but as things stand, the hosts should chase it down easily.

Nahid Rana’s rampage! The young pacer has been the star of the show, tearing through Pakistan's top and middle order to claim a five-wicket haul. His career best so far. Rana’s extra bounce and pace proved unplayable. He broke a cautious 41-run opening stand by removing debutants Sahibzada Farhan and Maaz Sadaqat in quick succession. However, credit to the captain, Mehidy Hasan Miraz, as well for keeping it tight from the other end as well. He bowled in tandem along with Rana in the 10-20 overs period that dismantled the Pakistani line-up.

Bangladesh put on a show - Nahid Rana leads the team with the ball in hand. What a fantastic spell from the young pacer. His effort has truly put the game to bed but Faheem Ashraf's cameo has given Pakistan something to fight for.  A clinical bowling display from Bangladesh have left Pakistan reeling at the Sher-e-Bangla National Stadium, as the visitors are bundled out for a meagre 114. After being put in to bat, Pakistan’s new-look top order failed to withstand a ferocious opening spell, leading to a dramatic collapse.

Commentary.Commentary: All in readiness now! We can see the Bangladesh players in a huddle before they spread out and take on the field. Sahibzada Farhan and Maaz Sadaqat are the two openers for Pakistan, both making their ODI debuts. Taskin Ahmed has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...

We are not far away from the start of the game, but before that, players from both sides make their way out to the middle and line up for their respective national anthems. It will be Pakistan's first, followed by that of Bangladesh.

PITCH REPORT - Former Bangladesh cricketer, Athar Ali Khan is pitchside. He says that there is a little bit of green tinge on top of the wicket. Adds that the bowlers will look to pitch it on the good length area to get some movement. Mentions that the square boundaries are 70 and 62 meters while the straight hit is 79 meters. He expects even bounce and reckons it will be good for both bowling and batting.

A winning start is crucial - Shaheen Afridi, the skipper of Pakistan, says he'd opt to bat first on this track. He also shares that they will have 4 debutants, therefore they will get the chance to bat freely without pressure, and support them. On the expectation on debutants he says that he is excited, having seen them perform well for the Shaheens and domestically. Afridi hopes they'll go on to have long careers with Pakistan. Afridi also believes a winning start is crucial as it gives him more freedom as captain, and he wants to just go with the flow and play their best cricket. After being asked that what would be a suitable target on the track, he replied that 270-280 would be a good target.

The players are excited for this series - Mehidy Hasan Miraz, the captain of Bangladesh, says they would like to bowl first as he feels the dew might come in the evening. Reckons that they have a very good bowling attack and hopes for some early wickets in the first 10 overs. Tells that they have experience with these conditions as they recently played a domestic tournament here. Mentions the players are excited for the series. Informs they are going with three pacers and two spinners.
Pakistan (Playing XI) - Sahibzada Farhan, Maaz Sadaqat, Shamyl Hussain, Mohammad Rizwan (WK), Salman Agha, Hussain Talat, Abdul Samad, Faheem Ashraf, Shaheen Afridi (C), Mohammad Wasim, Abrar Ahmed.

Bangladesh (Playing XI) - Mehidy Hasan Miraz (C), Tanzid Hasan, Saif Hassan, Najmul Hossain Shanto, Litton Das (WK), Tawhid Hridoy, Afif Hossain, Rishad Hossain, Taskin Ahmed, Mustafizur Rahman, Nahid Rana.
TOSS - Bangladesh have won the toss and elected to BOWL first.

A fresh chapter - Bangladesh also seeks to build momentum after the World Cup phase, which saw them navigate complex challenges including a withdrawal from scheduled matches in India. But surely they have got ample amount of time to focus on the future and think about the prosperity of the team. If we talk about their last ODI outing, it was a successful one with 2-1 series victory over the West Indies in October 2025 which also proves their strength in the longer format. The last time these two sides met in a One-Day International was during the 2023 World Cup, where Pakistan emerged victorious by seven wickets. However, Bangladesh holds a strong historical advantage at Mirpur, having previously achieved a clean sweep against the Men in Green on this very ground. So there is no doubt that this game will be a riveting one, but it will be interesting to see who gets the upper hand in this first clash of the series. Stay tuned for toss and team updates!

Focusing on the blueprint - Pakistan enters this series looking for redemption after a disappointing T20 World Cup campaign in India and Sri Lanka, where they failed to progress beyond the Super 8 stage. This underwhelming performance has led to a significant squad overhaul under head coach Mike Hesson, with six uncapped players included and high-profile players like Babar Azam, Mohammad Nawaz and also young prodigy like Saim Ayub notably missing the selection. Despite the recent T20 setback, Pakistan's ODI form remains formidable, having secured a 3-0 series sweep against Sri Lanka in November 2025, which they aim to carry into this tour as part of their long-term preparation.

Greetings folks - The first ODI between Bangladesh and Pakistan at the Sher-e-Bangla National Stadium in Mirpur, marks a pivotal return to the 50-over format for both nations. Significantly, this series is their first international encounter following the conclusion of the 2026 ICC Men's T20 World Cup phase, serving as a fresh start for teams looking to redefine their white-ball strategies.

Match intro - The cricketing world shifts its focus to Dhaka as Bangladesh hosts Pakistan for a three-match ODI series, starting March 11, 2026. This series represents a pivotal reset for both nations following the 2026 T20 World Cup. While Bangladesh enters the series after a period of internal transition and withdrawal from the global stage, Pakistan arrives with a radically revamped squad under the leadership of Shaheen Afridi. Pakistan’s 'New Era' Minus Babar - In a move that sent shockwaves through the cricketing community, the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) excluded Babar Azam from the ODI squad. The selection committee has signaled a hard pivot toward the future, naming six uncapped players (including the likes of  Maaz Sadaqat and Faisal Akram). With Shaheen Afridi at the helm, Pakistan is looking to shed its recent T20 World Cup baggage and build a blueprint for the 2027 ODI World Cup. Bangladesh’s Search for Stability - Led by Mehidy Hasan Miraz, the Tigers are looking to reclaim their status as 'giant killers' at home. The squad sees the return of Afif Hossain and the retention of Litton Das, despite the latter’s recent struggles. Playing in Mirpur, Bangladesh will rely on their spin-heavy arsenal and the passionate Dhaka crowd to unsettle a young Pakistani side. Form guide (Last 5 completed ODIS, most recent first) - BAN - WLWLL | PAK - WWWWL. How will the pitch play? The Shere Bangla National Stadium is notorious for its slow and low nature. Expect the ball to grip and turn from the first innings. Batting first has traditionally been the preferred choice in Mirpur to avoid chasing on a deteriorating surface, though the evening dew during a Day/Night fixture can sometimes assist the chasing side. What to expect? Despite the absence of Babar Azam, the pace trio of Shaheen Afridi, Haris Rauf, and Mohammad Wasim gives Pakistan a lethal edge. However, if the Mirpur pitch is a 'dust-bowl,' Bangladesh’s familiarity with the conditions could easily see them pull off a home win. Who are you backing for the win?
